issues.legal_issue: A compromise entered on behalf of a minor without the required court leave is voidable only at the minor’s instance, rather than a nullity.
material_facts: Two parties to the partition suit were minors and were represented by their guardian.
The guardian consented to a preliminary decree and the appointment of a commissioner without the court’s leave being recorded.
The agreement and decree concerned the suit in which the guardian represented the minors.
issues.conclusion: The failure to obtain the required leave did not make the agreement or preliminary decree a nullity; it made them voidable at the minors’ instance and not at the instance of other parties.
issues.legal_principle: Order 32, rules 7(1) and 7(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, protect minors by allowing them to avoid agreements or compromises made for them without the required leave. Non-compliance does not affect the court’s jurisdiction or render the agreement or decree void. Manohar Lal v. Jadu Nath Singh was noted as illustrating a proceeding to avoid a compromise decree. Chhabba Lal v. Kallu Lal, Jamna Bai v. Vasanta Rao, and Khiarajmal v. Daim were held inapplicable to the question of the effect of Order 32, rule 7(2).

predicates.civil_suit_involving_minor: A civil suit involved a party who was a minor and was represented by a guardian.
predicates.guardian_agreed_to_compromise: The guardian agreed on the minor’s behalf to a compromise or agreement concerning the suit.
predicates.required_court_leave_absent: The court did not grant and record the leave required for the guardian’s agreement.
predicates.compromise_and_decree_voidable_only_at_m: The agreement and resulting decree may be avoided by the minor, but not by another party on that ground.

issues.definition: When a guardian agrees to a compromise for a minor in a civil suit without the required court leave, the agreement and resulting decree are voidable only at the minor’s instance.

issues.legal_issue: A preliminary decree that was not appealed cannot be challenged for correctness or validity in an appeal from the final decree.
material_facts: A preliminary decree was passed by consent in a partition suit involving minor parties.
The minors’ guardian had consented without the required court leave.
The parties seeking to challenge the decree did not appeal from the preliminary decree.
They challenged its validity in an appeal from the final decree.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the preliminary decree was barred in the appeal from the final decree because no appeal had been brought against the preliminary decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 97 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, precludes a party who has not appealed from a preliminary decree from disputing its correctness in an appeal from the final decree. The bar includes a challenge to the decree’s legal validity, including a claim that it is voidable for non-compliance with Order 32, rule 7; otherwise, the purpose of section 97 would be frustrated.

predicates.appeal_from_final_decree: A party appealed from the final decree in a proceeding that had an earlier preliminary decree.
predicates.preliminary_decree_was_not_appealed: The party seeking to dispute the preliminary decree did not appeal from it.
predicates.challenge_targets_preliminary_decree: The party sought to dispute the correctness or legal validity of the preliminary decree in the later appeal.
predicates.challenge_barred_in_final_decree_appeal: The party cannot dispute the preliminary decree in the appeal from the final decree.

issues.definition: If a party appeals from a final decree without having appealed from the preliminary decree, a challenge to the preliminary decree is barred in that appeal.
